title: Chapter 23 — The Luxury Sale Process and White-Glove Delivery
intro: The consultation model, proposal craft, order-to-install, and the white-glove standard.

sections.title: The Proposal
sections.content:
Luxury sales require formal proposals — not counter quotes. A proposal includes product specifications, pricing, delivery timeline, installation requirements, coordination notes, and terms.

The proposal is a reflection of the service level the customer expects. It should be professional, complete, and accurate. Errors in a luxury proposal damage credibility disproportionately.

sections.title: White-Glove Delivery
sections.content:
Luxury delivery is not a truck dropping off a box. It is a coordinated installation with site protection, careful handling, professional setup, and a walkthrough with the homeowner.

The salesperson should be involved through delivery — confirming schedules, communicating with the customer, and ensuring the experience matches the price they paid.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating luxury process, ask:

Are proposals professional, complete, and error-free?
Is the delivery experience matching the luxury standard?
Is the salesperson involved through the entire order-to-install process — or handing off after the sale?
